leads.work: Gas settlements staff (Megan Parker, Elizabeth Hernandez, Tess Ray, Charlene Richmond) send the trader (Daren Farmer) one-off emails whenever a counterparty's price, volume or counterparty name differs from Sitara. Each one means digging through deal books and correcting Sitara by hand, often months late, and some need repeat reminders.
leads.why: These come in nearly every month: Mirant, Texaco, DEFS, ASTRA/ADTRA, Duke (with a follow-up nag), Houston Exploration ($222k), MGI, Tristar, Dow Cowtrap at $5.30 vs $5.31, and Global Octanes. Megan's 'For once this is not a Panenergy question' shows how routine they are. Payment deadlines are often at stake.

leads.work: Gas has flowed, but no deal exists in Sitara, a contract has expired, or a deal hasn't been released or extended, so it won't come across to Unify or settlements. Getting it fixed takes long forwarding chains across ENA, HPL and AEP after the HPL sale (contract extensions, adding meters, entering deals after the fact).
leads.why: The D&H Gas deal needed about 8 hops to extend the contract and still failed in Unify, then came back the next month. There are also the El Paso Merchant extension, the Equistar meter add, a deal 70550 release request, Huish meter 3425, missing AEP deals, the BP invoicing-entity question, TXU imbalance deals and Blue Dolphin June transport. Ownership confusion after the ENA-to-AEP transition keeps recurring.

leads.work: Volumes aren't actualized in Volume Management, which blocks payment through Unify (the Cowtrap/Blue Dolphin allocation with Spinnaker and Dow), so people chase each other by email to meet prompt-payment deadlines.
leads.why: Four messages over a few days ask 'who needs to talk to who', with a noon payment deadline. The gas had been nominated, tracked and balanced, but still didn't show.

leads.work: Old EPGT pipeline months are pathed and cleaned up by hand: interconnect paths, Unify/Quick Response error messages, and terminating inactive pools. This needs repeated status chasing and meetings with El Paso.
leads.why: Pathing requests from June 2000 were still unresolved in July 2001, with repeated follow-ups. In November the cleanup was only 70% done and involved hour-long calls with EPGT going through rejected line items.

leads.work: Hub Park and Lend balance information arrives late from EPGT after the transition from PG&E, so someone phones repeatedly to get balances.
leads.why: Mike was 'phoning them furiously' for daily balances. The message suggests disputing fees as a result.

leads.work: The real-time desk manager sends daily emails to the shift group listing long/short positions, prices, books (ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, ST-SW) and deal numbers. These often need correction emails, and the same deals are then re-entered in Enpower and CAPS by hand.
leads.why: These are near-daily broadcasts, including three emails in a row for one day ('One more time... No more messages'). There are also El Paso Electric lending set-ups each day and drafts handed to Kate to resend.

leads.work: Mail meant for Bill Williams goes to Bill Williams III and the other way round, so each one is forwarded and a correction requested from the sender.
leads.why: There are at least 9 cases in this batch (EES model, weather, FSP, PSR, Longview, contractor review, intern reviews). One message says 'Jeez this gets old'. Fixing the directory or address-book entries would remove this.

leads.work: Prior-month adjustments (PMAs) and revenue true-ups are researched by hand: missing offsetting deals, a $108k WBOM price change that never posted, TransAlta charges, and double-entered deals that had to be zeroed out.
leads.why: These are multi-week back-and-forth threads with Virginia Thompson and Fran Chang. The messages call it a 'flawed tool', and some settlement checks rely on pulling tapes.

leads.work: The real-time desk emails volume management and settlements by hand with congestion revenue, CAISO declines, misentered CISO schedules, cuts and generation-deviation allocations so they can be booked for the flash.
leads.why: These go out regularly, with hand-calculated revenue totals ($23,808, $54,059) and lists of schedule IDs.

leads.work: The night shift emails a daily EES model and real-time deal spreadsheet to EES settlements. The distribution list is maintained by hand and keeps going wrong, so the people who need it don't get it.
leads.why: The file is sent every day. There are several requests to change the recipient list (add Ainsley, remove Daniel, use the EES Power Settlements list).

leads.work: Every hour, traders phone Grays Harbor and Frontier for actual generation, then phone BPA, then initial a services sheet. They also call El Paso Electric dispatchers every hour. This will continue until the generators are automatically metered.
leads.why: It is a manual task done every hour, around the clock. BPA complained about inconsistent performance and threatened to recommend Enron be dropped from the service.

leads.work: The daily EPE reconciliation (CARP vs the El Paso model) is filled in by hand, and the sheet has to be completed even when there are no variances.
leads.why: This is a new daily step, and one shift has already been reminded for skipping it.

leads.work: The desk tracks the CAISO/FERC price cap and order changes by hand: emailing the CAISO rep to confirm the current cap, forwarding market notices, and interpreting penalty and outage-reporting rules. CAISO itself handles ancillary-service soft-cap payments as manual adjustments.
leads.why: There are many emails confirming the $91.87 cap and asking about a retroactive cap. CAISO says its manual soft-cap process is 'labor intensive, more prone to error'. Outage notices have to be phoned in to avoid penalties.

leads.work: Deal-entry errors in Enpower lead to disputes. There is a bi-weekly Enpower meeting on dispute thresholds, a swaps policy because swap disputes 'dragged on for months', and fixes for position-manager variances.
leads.why: This is a standing recurring meeting with recurring fixes for missing deal hours and variances.

leads.work: Annuities and inter-book transfers are entered by hand to compensate between books (ST-CALI to ST-WHOURLY, ST-WHourly to LT-NW, PGE transmission losses).
leads.why: Each one is negotiated and entered by email, with recalculation.

leads.work: Scheduling-system workarounds: CAPS outages, the FSP parallel run with CAPS, a 3AM customer-finals deadline for volume management's job, CAISO server downtime, and the move to the new OASIS site.
leads.why: These system changes cause repeated manual workarounds and re-briefings.

leads.work: Pacificorp (PACE) transmission reservations that were not withdrawn are being paid for, so traders must now email the manager each time a dispatcher removes a request.
leads.why: $57,000 was paid for transmission that never flowed. The new email step is manual.

leads.work: The CAISO ADS access cards and passwords expired, and the desk keeps chasing them.
leads.why: There is a possible violation of the participating generator agreement, and repeated follow-ups.

leads.work: Requests for audit support, tape pulls and deal verification (Arthur Andersen asking for third-party support on deals that have no executed contracts).
leads.why: Deals are confirmed by pulling tapes or calling around to settlements coordinators.

leads.work: HR and admin tasks: PEP reviewer minimums, self-evaluations, intern performance forms, slow access to the timekeeping system (14 business days), travel itinerary approval, and phone/headset orders.
leads.why: These are recurring review cycles, and access requests take a long time.

leads.work: Event and meeting RSVPs collected by email: customer trip slots, analyst meetings, golf tournament payment, ball games, training sign-ups.
leads.why: Repeated RSVP chasing.

leads.work: Outlook migration survey filled in by every Notes user, plus lists mapping traders to book admins that are kept by hand and redone when the desk reorganizes.
leads.why: A free-text survey goes out to hundreds of users. The book-admin list was compiled by hand, and the reorganization needs new books set up.

leads.work: Gas nominations and changes to rolled deals come in by email or fax: CP&L faxed noms, Imperial Sugar volume change, rolling Guadalupe deals and passing the new deal numbers on, Entex delivery cover, monthly volume confirmations for Mobil, and the Guadalupe monthly spreadsheet.
leads.why: This is a monthly manual exchange of nominations and deal numbers.

leads.work: Coordinating with Enron Canada and covering Sundance unit dispatch, including a manual offer resubmission by fax to the Alberta Power Pool.
leads.why: The process changed to a daily bid/offer, and coverage needs written instructions each time.

leads.work: Contractor insurance waiver notices go to a large distribution list that includes people who shouldn't be on it.
leads.why: Recipients ask to be removed. The original 209 requests suggest this is an ongoing contract-compliance process.

leads.work: Business-continuity planning: choosing critical staff and desks on the 30th floor for nominations if the new building fails.
leads.why: Each manager is asked by deadline how many desks they need, which suggests a planning exercise that recurs.

leads.work: A cuts-procedure reference manual and a list of trading-support tasks (collecting weather, derates, prices) to take the place of settlements work.
leads.why: This points to manual data gathering that could be automated.
